item.text: I have enough to synthesize. I’m not searching further; I’m turning the strongest positive and counterweight items into a compact note with claim-level mapping to 6B.1.

**Result**
- Net read: **yes, moderately strong**. In 2024 Scholz repeatedly framed government around wages, welfare-state protection, housing, pensions, child benefits, and municipal support. The main counterweights are fiscal constraints, Ukraine spending, and work-conditionality language, not clear evidence of propaganda or patronage.

**Accepted Claims**
- **Title:** `Germany's Scholz says he will keep social agenda in budget deal`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com  
  **Date:** 23 Jun 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/germanys-scholz-says-he-will-keep-social-agenda-in-budget-deal-3492843  
  **Claim:** Scholz said the coalition would stick to its social agenda, defend and further develop the welfare state, and keep negotiating welfare benefits and new housing inside the budget deal.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.1`

- **Title:** `Olaf Scholz nennt Prioritäten für den Haushalt 2024`  
  **Publisher:** Deutscher Bundestag  
  **Date:** 2023-06-?? page updated/archived in Bundestag record, used here as operative 2024 budget priority evidence  
  **URL:** https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2023/kw27-de-regierungsbefragung-954170  
  **Claim:** Scholz tied the budget to social cohesion through Bürgergeld, Wohngeld, higher child benefits, child supplement, and a children’s basic security plan, while also saying budgets should look beyond crisis management toward the country’s future.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.1`

- **Title:** `Summer press conference with Federal Chancellor Scholz`  
  **Publisher:** Federal Government  
  **Date:** 24 Jul 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/chancellor-summer-press-conference-2024-2301040  
  **Claim:** Scholz presented the welfare state, minimum wage enforcement, continuous basic-income support, and full pension entitlement after 45 years of contributions as core policy concerns, not side issues.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.1`

- **Title:** `Olaf Scholz nennt Prioritäten für den Haushalt 2024`  
  **Publisher:** Deutscher Bundestag  
  **Date:** 4 Dec 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2024/kw49-de-regierungsbefragung-1027922  
  **Claim:** Scholz said the government should help heavily indebted municipalities, expand social housing, and keep housing pressure from being solved by rhetoric alone; he also treated welfare-benefit and housing questions as live budget priorities.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.1`

**Counterweights**
- **Title:** `Germany's Scholz says he will keep social agenda in budget deal`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com  
  **Date:** 23 Jun 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/germanys-scholz-says-he-will-keep-social-agenda-in-budget-deal-3492843  
  **Claim:** The same reporting shows welfare had to be reconciled with military aid to Ukraine, tight borrowing rules, and a tougher stance on some benefit recipients, which makes the welfare posture conditional rather than unconditional.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.1`

- **Title:** `Summer press conference with Federal Chancellor Scholz`  
  **Publisher:** Federal Government  
  **Date:** 24 Jul 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/chancellor-summer-press-conference-2024-2301040  
  **Claim:** Scholz placed welfare-state stabilization alongside more money for the armed forces and further support for Ukraine, showing that welfare was central but not exclusive.  
  **Question IDs:** `6B.1`

**Search gap**
- I did not find direct evidence that Scholz used welfare policy as propaganda or patronage in 2024. The available material instead shows a real social-policy agenda constrained by fiscal rules, coalition bargaining, and security priorities.
